title: Ranveer Singh Becomes Ray-Ban's First Brand Ambassador in India
excerpt: The Bollywood star will front Ray-Ban and Ray-Ban Meta in India, headlining the 'Frame Your True Self' campaign as Meta's Gen 3 smart glasses go on sale starting at ₹44,300.
body:
• Ray-Ban has named Ranveer Singh its first-ever brand ambassador in India, covering both classic eyewear and the Ray-Ban Meta AI smart glasses.
  • The announcement was made on October 1, 2026, and launches the 'Frame Your True Self' campaign across digital, print, and retail channels nationwide.
  • It coincides with the India launch of Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3 smart glasses, priced from ₹44,300 in 27 colour-and-lens combinations — useful detail for readers buying or gifting in India this season.
  • The deal has drawn scrutiny over privacy: critics point to the glasses' built-in cameras, and a Dutch eyewear retailer suspended sales on October 2 amid recording concerns.

The announcement

Ray-Ban has appointed Bollywood actor Ranveer Singh as its first brand ambassador in India. The appointment covers both Ray-Ban's traditional eyewear and Ray-Ban Meta, the line of AI-powered smart glasses the brand builds with Meta, according to announcements carried by Storyboard18 and Bollywood Hungama.

https://x.com/MarketingMind_/status/2106043954982748610

Singh will lead the brand's upcoming communication in India under the campaign banner "Frame Your True Self," rolling out across digital, print, and retail channels nationwide, per FoneArena's report. The campaign visuals pair classic Ray-Ban frames with the latest smart glasses, leaning on the actor's reputation for expressive personal style.

"Ray-Ban has always stood for individuality, and that is something I have connected with for as long as I can remember," Singh said in the announcement. "Style, for me, has never been about following a fixed formula — it is about instinct, mood and having the freedom to express every version of yourself."

"Ray-Ban's incredible legacy of people who have done things their own way, along with Meta's vision of building AI glasses for everyone — I'm excited to be a part of that story in India."

— Ranveer Singh, actor

Context & background

This is not Singh's first engagement with Meta. The actor has collaborated with the company on several previous projects, and Ray-Ban noted that history as part of the rationale for the appointment, per t2Online.

The brand pairing is also a meeting of two legacies. Ray-Ban, owned by EssilorLuxottica, brings nearly nine decades of eyewear design — the Aviator style turns 90 this year, marked by a limited-edition release — while Meta supplies the wearable technology stack: cameras, microphones, speakers, and its Meta AI assistant. Globally, Singh joins a roster that includes BLACKPINK's Jennie and Formula 1 champion Lewis Hamilton, according to Bollywood Hungama.

The timing rides a strong phase of Singh's acting career. The Dhurandhar franchise has generated significant box-office attention and discussion around his performances, keeping him visible well beyond Indian cinema audiences.

Impact & analysis

The appointment arrives alongside the India launch of Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3, the latest generation of the AI glasses. Priced from ₹44,300 in India, Gen 3 brings a slimmer design, up to nine hours of battery life, and a customisable action button that opens Meta AI directly, per Storyboard18's coverage. The line comes in 27 colour-and-lens combinations across three styles — Aviator, Zena, and Wayfarer — with a 12-megapixel camera recording 3K Ultra HD video and a six-microphone array the company says cuts more than 90% of background noise. Meta also announced plans to bring its Muse personal AI agent to the glasses.

But the technology has a harder sell in front of it. Singh's appointment has triggered social media debate over the privacy implications of camera-equipped glasses, with critics arguing they could normalise recording people without their knowledge or consent. The concerns are not India-specific: on October 2, Dutch eyewear retailer Hans Anders suspended sales of Ray-Ban Meta glasses in the Netherlands and Belgium over covert-recording worries, according to Khel Ja. Meta's response is hardware-level — a built-in LED indicator that lights up during recording and cannot be disabled, with the camera disabled entirely if the light is covered or damaged.

Diaspora angle

For the Indian diaspora, the significance runs in both directions. A Bollywood star leading a global AI hardware push in India signals how central the Indian market has become to Meta's wearables strategy — and diaspora households, already heavy adopters of smart devices, often set the tone for what Indian relatives eventually buy. The ₹44,300 entry price also matters practically: diaspora shoppers buying in India this festive and wedding season will find the Gen 3 line on shelves alongside the classic frames.

What's next

Watch how the "Frame Your True Self" campaign performs across retail, and whether the privacy debate in Europe bleeds into the India launch. The arrival of Meta's Muse AI agent on the glasses could be the next inflection point — if the software delivers genuinely useful hands-free assistance, the price tag becomes easier to justify; if not, Ray-Ban risks leaning on celebrity shine to move a gadget people distrust.
